marks.gloss_en: since it teaches 'the tooth is muad to eat', the clause must speak of the injured party's courtyard (shen is exempt in the public domain) -- and 'the animal is not muad' there means it pays half for the unusual
the Rabbanan: keren-type damage in the injured party's courtyard is unusual (משונה) and pays half damages
R. Tarfon: unusual keren-type damage in the injured party's courtyard pays full damages
Shmuel to Rav Yehuda: sharp one, leave the mishnah and follow me -- the first clause is the Rabbanan and the later clause is R. Tarfon
